script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The passage says the arrival is like a column of smoke, not that there is a column of smoke. It also does not say Solomon is riding into his wedding.
Identifying Solomon as Israel's king is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Naaman's identification as an Aramean army commander needs a reference to 2 Kings 5:1; the cited verse, 5:9, does not identify his role.
The poem says the warriors are prepared for the terror of the night. It does not say they are covered in daylight too.
The poem does not say the warriors need no trumpet or that they stay ready at all times.
The passage identifies the silver posts and gold base, but does not say the silver and gold are on the outside.
The passage does not say the scene takes place in Zion or that the whole town gets a front-row seat.
The explanation is flat and repetitive. It restates the invitation and adds only that the poem does not say why the daughters are called.
Calling the parade for the daughters of Zion adds a purpose the passage does not give.
Identifying David as Israel's king is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not say the groom has finished looking.
The groom continues describing his bride after verse 7, so this is not the end of his description.
The cookie comparison does not make clear sense: a cookie needing a whole batch to impress Papa does not match the action of a single glance capturing a heart.
The winds are called to spread the fragrance. The verse does not say it goes in every direction or that the garden is about to be noticed.
The verse invites the beloved to taste the fruit; it does not say he does so.
The explanation is flat and repeats the answer without adding a distinct insight or Papa's personality.
The next verse records his arrival, but the passage does not say how quickly he came or how many times he was asked.
The arrival appears in the next verse, but calling it quick service adds a timing the passage does not give.
The passage does not mention a table or say everyone gets a seat. This is also not the end of the poem.
The passage does not mention a table, and the poem does not end at Song of Solomon 5:1.
This is not the end of the poem. The passage also does not say the feast is ready or that nobody is standing around.
